A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfoSearch research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of retrieval and reranking models on InfoSearch, including aggregate results in Tables 2–3 and detailed results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original model evaluations in Tables 1–2 and Appendix E. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical results.

M1.justification: The seven-stage benchmark construction procedure and dense, point-wise and list-wise retrieval procedures remain the same. Additional construction prompts document existing operations; they do not establish a changed algorithm. The WISE definition change is assessed under E3 and T1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six document attributes and original, instructed and reversely instructed modes. Data sources, condition values and dataset examples match; the relocated statistics retain 600 core queries, 1,598 queries in each instruction mode and 6,392 documents.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches across both aggregate tables and all six detailed result tables. v2 Table 1 separates existing list-wise entries into fine-tuned and instructional zero-shot groups, without adding or removing evaluated models.

E3.justification: Section 2.3 revises WISE's within-top-K reward weighting from a linear rank-difference term to a square-root term. This is a reported evaluation-metric change, although the PDFs do not establish recomputation. Dataset sizes, K=20, E5-Mistral top-100 reranking and other stated evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D/Figure 5 numerically explores WISE rewards across original and instructed rank pairs, including the top-K boundary. This adds a limited examination of metric behavior. Existing model comparisons, dimension analyses and dataset examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. The new reward-function sampling does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All model-result entries match between v1 Tables 2–3 and 15–20 and v2 Tables 1–2 and 17–22. v2 adds numerical reward samples in Figure 5, such as 0.782 for original rank 20 and instructed rank 1. These are illustrative metric values, not new model-performance gains.

T1.justification: The WISE reward branch changes from (1-(Rori-Rins)/K)/sqrt(Rins) in v1 Equation 7 to (1-sqrt(Rori-Rins)/K)/sqrt(Rins) in v2 Equation 4. This is a non-equivalent revision to one part of the formal definition. SICR, the remaining WISE branches and the relocated prior-metric formulas are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the six-attribute InfoSearch benchmark, SICR and WISE, and evidence that existing models inadequately follow instructions. The abstract is condensed, but the introduction retains the claims about reranking superiority and benefits from instruction-aware fine-tuning and model size.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning joint generative training, contextual reranking, audience/format difficulties and limitations of existing metrics are retained. The point-wise versus list-wise discussion is shortened without changing its explanation. No substantive new applicability boundary or limitation is introduced.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit prompts for keyword-condition generation, length rewriting and hard-negative generation in Tables 3, 6 and 8. It also specifies which dimensions chiefly require rewriting and mentions multiple screening rounds. Conversely, v1 Table 5's core-query generation prompt is omitted. These are documentation changes, not evidence that construction was rerun.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds discussion of PIR's perspective-sensitive retrieval and positions InfoSearch against MAIR's 126-task benchmark. Both additions have unresolved question-mark citations, while the bibliography itself is unchanged. Existing related-work positioning is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes existing exposition: Section 2's construction details become Appendix A.1–A.7, prompt descriptions are integrated there, and the detailed critique of earlier metrics moves to Appendix B. The abstract, introduction and part of Section 4 are condensed. Author/affiliation text changes and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds the reward heatmap and new prompt tables, expands and reformats existing prompt displays, relocates dataset statistics and splits Table 1's list-wise block into two groups. Existing Figures 1–4 and the principal result-table designs are retained. Conference headers and page layout also change.

improvement.justification: The reorganized appendices and added construction prompts improve documentation, although the core-query prompt is lost. However, v2 changes the central WISE equation without explaining its relationship to the unchanged reported scores, and new Figure 5 displays 0.100 beyond rank 20 whereas Equation 4 specifies 0.01. The PDFs do not resolve whether the formula revision corrects the computation or changes intended scoring. These ambiguities prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
